feasibility.reason: The video gives a thirty-minute soak, but LECA preparation and reservoir depth are vague. Applying a small-corm demonstration to a heavy plant requires substantial adaptation.

[0:19] I need to check the roots… that’s the only way to know if it can be saved.
[0:36] It’s still alive… I can feel it.
[0:42] Which means there’s a chance—let’s bring it back.
[0:57] This method has never failed me…
[1:05] Just 5 drops of hydrogen peroxide per 7 oz of water — it disinfects and oxygenates at the same time while the corm soaks.
[1:13] Now it just needs 30 minutes…
[1:18] This method has already helped me save a Spider Plant — just look at how well it’s doing now.
[1:31] And this little Anthurium… it grew beautiful new leaves and strong roots almost from nothing.
[1:43] Why this method?
[1:46] LECA retains moisture while still allowing air to reach the roots—this means less rot and much easier watering control.
[2:05] This is called semi-hydroponics.
[2:16] Now I just need to keep a small water level at the bottom at all times.
[2:28] I place it in a bright spot with indirect light… and now all that’s left is to be patient and watch it recover.
